title: Yardbook vs Jobber (2026): Free Plan vs Paid, Real Prices
description: Yardbook vs Jobber for lawn care: Yardbook's free plan and 1% payment fee vs Jobber's per-user plans, routing, QuickBooks and trials, from vendor pages.
h1: Yardbook vs Jobber for lawn care and landscaping
body:
Yardbook and Jobber come up together when a lawn care or landscaping operator picks a first system. Yardbook has a free Starter plan with scheduling, estimates, invoices and routing, and charges a 1% Yardbook fee on online payments until you upgrade. Jobber has no free plan, but it publishes a per-user price ladder, and we track it across all five trades we cover. Numbers come from Yardbook pricing (checked 2026-11-04) and Jobber pricing (checked 2026-11-08). Anything a vendor doesn't publish is marked unknown.

{{table:yardbook,jobber}}

Plans and prices

  • Yardbook: Starter is free and includes scheduling, estimates, invoices, routing, snow removal and lot measurement. Business is $34.99/mo and waives the 1% Yardbook payment fee. Enterprise is $49.99/mo and adds QuickBooks sync. On free and trial accounts, online payments carry Stripe's fees plus a 1% Yardbook fee. Yardbook doesn't publish a per-user price or a separate annual rate. Its pricing page lists web, desktop and Android app access and doesn't mention iOS.
  • Jobber: Core is $29/mo billed annually, $39/mo on a 1-year commitment, or $49/mo with no commitment, for 1 user. Connect is $99/$119/$139 and Grow $149/$169/$199 for 1 user (annual / 1-year monthly / no commitment), with 5-, 10- and 15-user tiers. Extra users are $29/mo each. Card payments are 2.9% + 30¢ online. The 14-day trial runs on Grow and needs no credit card.

Where the features sit

FeatureYardbookJobber
RoutingOn Starter (free)Connect and up ($99/mo billed annually); not on Core
QuickBooksEnterprise only ($49.99/mo)QuickBooks Online and Xero sync on Connect and up
Chemical trackingListed; multi-step chemical programs on Business and upunknown (not listed on the pricing page)
Online bookingunknown (customized lead capture on Business)Yes
Payment feesStripe fees + 1% Yardbook fee on free/trial accounts; Yardbook fee waived on Business and Enterprise2.9% + 30¢ online; 2.7% + 30¢ Tap to Pay; ACH 1%

When Yardbook's 1% fee costs more than upgrading

On the free plan, Yardbook takes 1% of online payments on top of Stripe's fees. Business costs $34.99/mo and removes that 1%. So once you take more than about $3,499 a month in online payments, Business costs less than the 1% fee (1% of $3,499 is $34.99). This is simple arithmetic from the published prices, before Stripe's own fees. At $5,000/mo of online payments, the Yardbook fee alone would be $50/mo on Starter.

What a solo operator pays

  • Cheapest start: Yardbook Starter, $0/mo plus the 1% fee on online payments, with routing included.
  • Routing plus QuickBooks: Yardbook Enterprise is $49.99/mo. Jobber Connect is $99/mo billed annually or $139/mo with no commitment.
  • Jobber's lowest price: Core is $29/mo billed annually ($49/mo no commitment), but it doesn't include routing.

Which should you pick?

  • Solo lawn or landscaping operator on a tight budget: Yardbook. The free plan covers scheduling, invoices and routing.
  • You run iPhones in the field: Yardbook's pricing page doesn't mention an iOS app, so confirm with Yardbook before you commit.
  • Several trades, or you plan to add crew: Jobber. Its per-user ladder and 5-user tiers are published. {{aff:jobber|See Jobber plans}}
